newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine five-year coupon at 12.50 percent.
newsitem.headline: Philippine five-year coupon at 12.50 percent.

text.p: The coupon rate on the Philippines' five-year fixed rate Treasury bonds plunged to 12.5 percent at an auction on Tuesday compared with 14.5 percent at the previous auction held in November last year, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The average rate tumbled to 12.411 percent from 14.423, with the low at 12.375 and the high at 12.60 percent.
The auction drew bids worth 14.150 billion pesos, of which 3.5 billion pesos were awarded.
Traders said they had expected the coupon rate to be at a higher 12.75 percent.
However, "the market is awash with money," a foreign bank dealer said, adding that insurance firms continue to have big requirements for long-term placements.
"Rates have moved considerably down since the last auction in November," another said.
Interest rates have fallen sharply since the start of the year after the Central Bank cut reserve requirements for banks by one percentage point on January 3.
Also, banks' liquidity had risen after they stayed away from term reverse repos which had been charged a 20 percent tax.
